elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Trigger reads "where TrueLink processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Client, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger reaches every category of Client data rather than selected named data types (e.g. Client Content or Credit Data).

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance to Client on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000 in the inserted clause exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000 in the inserted clause exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: The rule is correctly scored as missing: the Agreement contains no insurance, coverage, policy, certificate or workers' compensation obligation, and the insertion is placed in the miscellaneous section as the redline guidance directs.

All six preferred elements appear in a single inserted sentence pair with the exact coverage lines and amounts; the conditional cyber trigger is drafted to catch any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, so it does not fail the data-category test.

Minimality holds: the drafter inserted only the insurance obligation and omitted the model-language extras (the one-year survival tail and "at its own expense"), and no word of the retained Force Majeure clause (Section 30) was altered or deleted.

Intent is preserved: nothing in the insertion contradicts the force majeure allocation, no defined term is created or left undefined, and no cross-reference is disturbed. "Client" and "TrueLink" track the Agreement's own defined parties.
The margin comment properly holds the E&O USD 1,000,000 / cyber USD 2,000,000 fallback in reserve rather than drafting it, so the operative language sits cleanly at the preferred level.
